articles.title: City and co all huffing and puffing to keep pace with the Arsenal title juggernaut | Jonathan Wilson
articles.dek: Recent wobbles aside, Mikel Arteta’s supreme side are widening the gap to Liverpool, Brighton and Sunday’s vexed rivals Two draws in a row. Three draws and a shootout…
articles.description: Recent wobbles aside, Mikel Arteta’s supreme side are widening the gap to Liverpool, Brighton and Sunday’s vexed rivals Two draws in a row. Three draws and a shootout defeat in their past eight games. Three of their past four games have seen a second-half drop-off. Are Arsenal wobbling? Might there actually be some prospect of a title race? It says something for how dominant they have appeared that even slight suggestions they may not be infallible are being seized on in the desperate hope there might be a title race this season. Mikel Arteta may have looked frustrated on the touchline against Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday but his positive words post-match were surely broadly true. It might not quite have been the “brilliant” performance he claimed but, as at Newcastle last Saturday, Arsenal would have won comfortably had they not missed a string of first-half chances. “The execution,” he said, “can be better, but everything in between was really good.” That they hadn’t taken more chances, he explained, was a matter of “luck … composure … quality”. Continue reading...

articles.dek: Leeds are becoming the poster boys of evolutionary progress in the Premier League. In their second season back in the top flight, they sit sixth after almost a third of…
articles.description: Leeds are becoming the poster boys of evolutionary progress in the Premier League. In their second season back in the top flight, they sit sixth after almost a third of the season, having made light work of a meek Coventry. Sean Longstaff’s double after Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s opener were more than enough, although Leeds should have had plenty more. Guided by Daniel Farke’s efficient and effective tactics and careful recruitment, without breaking the bank, they are rapidly becoming one of the league’s least favoured opponents thanks to their physicality and technical ability. They are yet to lose here this season and never looked like relinquishing that statistic on Saturday, as fans start to dream of European qualification. Continue reading...

articles.title: Jørgen Strand Larsen: ‘Dad and I have been best mates since I was a kid – that’s not going to change’
articles.dek: Striker determined to raise prostate cancer awareness after father, who scored goals for fun at amateur level in Norway, received terminal diagnosis It is a fresh Friday…
articles.description: Striker determined to raise prostate cancer awareness after father, who scored goals for fun at amateur level in Norway, received terminal diagnosis It is a fresh Friday afternoon at Selhurst Park and, after posing for a couple of pictures in front of the red and blue Holmesdale End, Jørgen Strand Larsen holds a scarf overhead in true new-signing style. This is not the last step before a routine announcement, nor is this a run-of-the-mill club, his manicured moustache a giveaway. The Crystal Palace and Norway striker has joined forces with Prostate Cancer UK to raise awareness of the disease after his father, Atle Wester, was given a terminal diagnosis this year. Strand Larsen arrives after a recovery session following Thomas Frank’s first victory since taking charge. He devotes more than an hour to learning more about a subject close to his heart, meeting Dr Matthew Hobbs, the charity’s research director, before a round-table conversation with Mark Bright, a Palace ambassador, and a couple of fans with links to the cause. Continue reading...

articles.title: Steph Catley celebrates milestone as Matildas battle past Colombia in feisty Canberra friendly
articles.dek: Catley wore the armband for Australia in her 150th cap Goals to Alanna Kennedy and Caitlin Foord capped off a 3-1 win Steph Catley has celebrated her 150th appearance for…
articles.description: Catley wore the armband for Australia in her 150th cap Goals to Alanna Kennedy and Caitlin Foord capped off a 3-1 win Steph Catley has celebrated her 150th appearance for Australia in style, playing a key role in the Matildas’ go-ahead goal as they kicked away in the second half to secure a 3-1 win over Colombia. After Alanna Kennedy and Linda Caicedo netted inside the opening 15 minutes, Catley’s 59th-minute corner ricocheted off Daniela Arias’s back to put Australia into the ascendancy, before Caitlin Foord struck three minutes later to secure a match-winning cushion. articles.title: Basque to the future: Andoni Iraola fired up for first Merseyside derby
articles.dek: Liverpool head coach sees parallels with Athletic v Sociedad derby as he comes up against his old foe David Moyes “I haven’t lived this derby,” Andoni Iraola…
articles.description: Liverpool head coach sees parallels with Athletic v Sociedad derby as he comes up against his old foe David Moyes “I haven’t lived this derby,” Andoni Iraola acknowledged, and yet he already feels it. A former Athletic Bilbao captain coming up against an ex-Real Sociedad head coach needs no instruction on the importance of winning a derby, whether in the Basque country or on Merseyside. But this week, as the Liverpool head coach approaches his first experience of the latter, there has been no escape. “It has been very easy for me here,” says Iraola of his five months on Merseyside. “Family-wise we have settled in really well. People here are very friendly, they love to talk to you but in a very respectful way. This week there has been a lot [of interaction with Liverpool fans], especially with playing big games against United and Everton. ‘We need to win, we need to win,’ they say.” Continue reading...

articles.title: The Renéessance is over but Arsenal’s chaotic cycle will go on without further change | Suzanne Wrack
articles.dek: Renée Slegers’ exit, 18 months on from European glory, was inevitable but much of the blame lies with those higher up The Renéessance is over. Three down, how many more…
articles.description: Renée Slegers’ exit, 18 months on from European glory, was inevitable but much of the blame lies with those higher up The Renéessance is over. Three down, how many more to go? The exit of Arsenal manager, Renée Slegers, 18 months after delivering European glory was somewhat inevitable, her position made untenable after six home draws in six games and just 15 points from 11 games, but will it solve the Gunners’ problems? There were high expectations in north London prior to the season, after difficult starts in back-to-back WSL campaigns put them outside a real title challenge within the opening few games.
